description: Wood for Life, a Collaborative Partnership to Provide Wood to the Navajo Nation and Hopi Tribe is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. The Wood for Life partnership (WFL) was developed as a collaborative effort between a network of organizations in northern Arizona to respond to the need for firewood by making wood from forest restoration treatments on NFS lands available to communities on the Navajo Nation and Hopi Tribal lands. Coverage: Arizona (2024). The toolkit gives Arizona as the location, 2024 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
